title: Measure before laying out nested nodes
summary: Separate graph identity, layout and DOM measurement.
objectives: Keep parent identity separate from measured size.
Explain why delayed measurement needs an explicit state.

sources.title: Vue lifecycle hooks
sources.basis: DOM effects belong after mounting; dispose subscriptions on unmount. The exercise is a pure layout model, not a browser integration.

sections.title: Identity is available before dimensions
paragraphs: A child can refer to a stable parent ID before the browser measures the parent. Do not invent a width when the parent is missing or unmeasured.
Keep the graph record independent of DOM references. A renderer can report dimensions later without changing graph identity.

sections.title: Deterministic layout and cleanup
paragraphs: For two synthetic children with heights 20 and 30, place them at y=0 and y=28 with an 8-unit gap. Recomputing should produce the same result.
A real component must also test resize, removal, SSR and unmount cleanup. This lesson does not establish that a particular graph module implements those cases.

exercise.instruction: Run the measured-layout exercise for missing dimensions, two children and repeated computation.
exercise.expected: Missing measurement produces pending; measured children have positions 0 and 28; input state stays unchanged.

limitations: Pure TypeScript exercise only; no graph editor or DOM integration is tested here.
Research guidance; not a claim that a released module supports these requirements.
